newsitem.title: UK: Kingfisher Q1 sales rise 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Kingfisher Q1 sales rise 8.0 pct.

text.p: UK stores group Kingfisher Plc said on Wednesday that sales in the 13 weeks ended May 3 rose by 8.0 percent on a comparable stores basis and by 10.1 percent overall.
The sales rise matched the rate of growth in Kingfisher's last full financial year ended February 1, when like-for-like sales rose by 7.4 percent and total sales by 10.1 percent.
Total sales in the first 13 weeks were 1.362 billion stg.

Commenting on the performance Kingfisher Chief Executive, Sir Geoffrey Mulcahy, said in a statement, "We have made a good start to the year, with the strong sales performance of B&Q and Comet the highlights. Whilst encouraging, it is only the first quarter and too early to start drawing conclusions as Kingfisher is heavily dependent on the second half.
"What is certain is that our markets remain very competitive."

B&Q, the UK's market leader in do-it-yourself goods, increased sales by 21.8, or 14.4 percent on a like-for-like basis. Kingfisher said this represented a continuation of the strong growth of last year.
Warehouse sales continued to grow at around previous rates, while Supercentre sales were significantly ahead. In particular, gardening sales were boosted by the fine early Spring weather.

Sales at electrical goods chain Comet continued to grow strongly, by 34.2 percent or 10.4% like-for-like. The overall performance was boosted by the inclusion of stores still trading as Norweb Retail, without which the rate of growth was 17.6 percent.

Darty, the market-leading French electrical retailer, grew total sales by 1.5 percent in local currency terms, a fall of 0.2 percent like-for-like. Kingfisher said this sales performance was ahead of the market, but the strength of sterling led to total turnover declining by 15.1 percent after currency translation.
Superdrug pharmacy sales grew by 9.8 percent, or 6.3 percent like-for-like.
Woolworths continued to build on last year's performance and grew sales by 6.8 percent, or 6.2 percent like-for-like.
